objective: Exploratory experiment. With exact bond distances (least cycles through two edges of the plane dual), measure the circles of the parity laws on three right-triangle substitution tilings: the pinwheel (Conway's cut of the 1:2 triangle, mirror pairs, orientations growing by four per level), the frame-consistent cut of the same triangle into the same five copies (altitude, then midpoints: one frame, four orientations), and the 1:1 triangle halved by its altitude (the periodic tetrakis triangulation). For knots at tile corners and knots on tiles, record anisotropy and low Fourier harmonics of the radial profile at radii 8 to 128. Predictions: the 1:1 laws keep their polygons (square, anisotropy sqrt 2; octagon); the pinwheel laws round off; the frame-consistent laws are not forced round.
status: Closed, supported (exploratory, PINWHEEL-ROUND-20261107-001B-E001): measured circles of right-triangle substitution laws, exact bond distances, radii 8 to 128. The 1:1 controls converge to their exact polygons (corner law 1.124 vs octagon 1.118; tile law 1.410 vs square 1.414). The pinwheel corner law rounds off (anisotropy 1.106 -> 1.030, 4-fold harmonic 0.014 -> 0.0001); the pinwheel tile law falls 1.33 -> 1.08 (unresolved by the frozen 1.06 threshold). The frame-consistent cut does not round off: its 4-fold harmonic grows to 0.085 and 0.100 (anisotropy 1.19-1.27, unresolved by the frozen rule). Pinwheel orientations within R: 13, 19, 20, 24, 28 for R = 8 to 128.
title: Measured circles of right-triangle substitution laws
